Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class WorldEditChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.WorldEditChecks
public final class WorldEditChecks extends Object
World edits and their notifications, observed through the world's native game-event dispatcher, and the rules that keep a gesture or automation from writing where it should not: build height, entity obstruction, the world border, and waterlogging. Automation scenarios take the loader's GameTestScaffold.Automation view.

    • playerCausedCleanupCarriesThePlayer

      public static void playerCausedCleanupCarriesThePlayer(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      To reproduce: in a claim that admits a player but denies [SomeStacks], extract the last item from a temporary Storage, Singles, and Bar Stack, and toggle an empty permanent Storage pile back to temporary. Each empty block is removed on the player's behalf, so the claim allows it and logging mods record the player. Extracting one of two Storage items by hand and the other by automation before settlement attributes the cleanup to [SomeStacks] instead, so that claim keeps the empty block.

    • breakingAStackChargesItsCleanupToTheBreaker

      public static void breakingAStackChargesItsCleanupToTheBreaker(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      To reproduce: in a claim that admits a player but denies [SomeStacks], stack two Bar Stacks with one bar per layer in the lower block holding up one bar in the upper block, and break the lower block by hand. The upper bar falls and its emptied block is removed on the player's behalf, so the claim allows it and logging mods record the player. Then build a temporary Storage pile three blocks high with one stack in each block and break its base: the two remaining stacks settle into the lower block and the emptied top is removed, again under the player. Removing the lower block any other way, such as /setblock or an explosion, charges the same cleanup to [SomeStacks].

    • placementGrowthAndCleanupNotify

      public static void placementGrowthAndCleanupNotify(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick click)
      To reproduce: put a sculk sensor near a floor, V-place Storage holding dirt, fill its slots, and have a hopper deposit stone to grow it. Extract the stone and let settlement trim the upper block. Each structural edit produces its placement or destruction vibration, subject to ordinary sculk filtering. Inventory edits alone do not produce these structural events.

    • checkedPlacementPlacesInBoundsAndRejectsOutsideBuildHeight

      public static void checkedPlacementPlacesInBoundsAndRejectsOutsideBuildHeight(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      Internal checked-placement test: place stone at an in-bounds position, then try a position one below the minimum build height. Only the in-bounds call succeeds. The out-of-world call has no direct player reproduction.

      Nearest manual check: select Storage and V-place an admissible item against a floor in bounds, then try to grow a stack beyond the world's upper build limit. No out-of-bounds block should appear.

    • storageGrowthAnswersToProtectionInSimulationAndCommit

      public static void storageGrowthAnswersToProtectionInSimulationAndCommit(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
      World-border fixture: fill one Storage block, first confirm a free headroom offer has capacity, then move the border to exclude the target and try simulation and commit. Both refuse the entire four-item offer without growth or input mutation.

      To reproduce, allow height above one, fill a Storage pile, and use /worldborder center and /worldborder set to exclude its prospective growth position. Offer admissible items to first headroom through slot-addressing automation. No upper block appears. Restore the original border after the check; dry-run results require simulation/abort support.

    • storageGrowthRejectsAnObstructingEntityInSimulationAndCommit

      public static void storageGrowthRejectsAnObstructingEntityInSimulationAndCommit(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
      To reproduce: allow height above one, fill one Storage block, and confine a cow in the prospective upper block's first occupied position.     • completedShapesDistinguishOccupiedCellsFromEmptySpace

      public static void completedShapesDistinguishOccupiedCellsFromEmptySpace(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal obstruction-shape check: a cow overlaps one edge of the target position. Full and occupied-edge shapes are obstructed; empty shapes and distant Singles/Bar positions are clear. No block placement or deposit is performed.

      Nearest manual check: hold a cow at one edge of a destination and attempt first placement of Singles or Bar into occupied-edge and clear positions. Only shapes overlapping the cow should prevent placement.

    • outsideTheBorder

      public static void outsideTheBorder(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Runnable action)
      Runs action with the world border moved off the test structure, and restores it before returning. The border is level-wide state, but the move and the restore both happen inside this one synchronous call, so no other test observes it moved.
